CLIMATE NOTE

NOTE
Longwave pattern continues to support dry and stable conditions across the Great Lakes today as the Mississippi Valley ridge flattens eastward. This unfolds as the first in a series of progressive Pacific shortwaves lift out of the Rockies and into the Upper Midwest. The 586 dam 500 mb ridge is progged to track up the Ohio River and into southern Appalachia by this evening. Expect continued lower column anticyclonic influence to offer sustained weak subsidence with high static stability, but a confluent stream of milder Gulf-modified air will hold just west of southwest Lower Michigan. Forecast soundings highlight a dry column, with PWATs dropping to around 0.25 inches. Insufficient boundary-layer saturation for a diurnal cumulus response, but given the upstream wave, high cirrus should spill in aloft with varying density. Thermodynamically, 850 mb temperatures appear relatively steady today, if not marginally warmer than Tuesday. Daytime highs should reach the mid-upper 50s. Upper level clouds thicken tonight while lower tropospheric theta-e advection works in late tonight from the west. The speed max is expected to sharpen as it cross The UP and into Ontario Thursday, featuring a vertically stacked area of low pressure through 300 mb. Southeast Michigan becomes positioned between the surface low over central Ontario and high pressure over the Mid-Atlantic. This leads to a tightening pressure gradient resulting in an uptick in prevailing winds. Tenuous stability should limit the window of opportunity for lower column winds to effectively mix down and produce higher magnitude gusts. However, during the diurnal peak, should mixing depths tap into the 3-5 kft AGL layer, some 30-40 knots of flow would be available for gusts in excess of 30 mph. The low's extended cold front washes out over central Lower, which prevents a material wind shift toward the west and maintains a dry forecast. The next ridge axis works in Thursday night into Friday offering a more zonal orientation aloft. The jet resides to the north into the weekend as the next Pacific trough works through the Four Corners. The next chance for rain comes Sunday as the embedded Pacific wave ejects across the Plains. Lots of moving parts to contend with given the subtropical storm along the southern Atlantic coast and a meandering low moving south across the Canadian Prairies that interferes with the jet pattern. Highs rise into the 60s during the weekend. Colder weather returns early next week. && .MARINE... As low pressure exits the northern Plains late Wednesday, an increase in the pressure gradient over Lake Huron looks to lead to a modest increase in southwest winds, despite the mild air mass (850 mb temps of 5 to 7 C) working through. Thus, another round of Small Craft Advisories appears likely for tonight into Thursday. There still does not appear to be enough of an increase in low level moisture to support any rain activity through the workweek. A ridge axis tracking through on Friday will lead to light winds. Another strong low is expected to track just northwest of Lake Superior Friday night, allowing at least moderate south-southwest winds to develop by Saturday. Forecast uncertainty ramps up to finish the weekend into Monday, as ensemble members and operational medium range models differ on whether a secondary low will develop over the Midwest and track through northern Michigan. A handful of solutions suggest marginal northwest gales could come into play Sunday night in the wake of the low. && .PREV DISCUSSION... Issued at 955 PM EST Tue Nov 17 2026 AVIATION... Light southwesterly winds tonight as cirrus streams in from the west. Model trends have backed off on radiative fog development late tonight-early Wednesday morning so opted to limit mentions to tempo groups of high MVFR-low VFR vsbys. Any shallow fog that does develop burns off after sunrise with daytime Wednesday marked by modest (~10kt) SW winds and continued high cloud. For DTW... Patchy shallow fog possible early Wednesday morning. Anything that does develop burns off after ~12-13Z. DTW THRESHOLD PROBABILITIES... * None. && .DTX WATCHES/WARNINGS/ADVISORIES... MI...None. Lake Huron...None. Lake St Clair...None. .DISCUSSION...

Longwave pattern continues to support dry and stable conditions 
across the Great Lakes today as the Mississippi Valley ridge 
flattens eastward. This unfolds as the first in a series of 
progressive Pacific shortwaves lift out of the Rockies and into the 
Upper Midwest. The 586 dam 500 mb ridge is progged to track up the 
Ohio River and into southern Appalachia by this evening. Expect 
continued lower column anticyclonic influence to offer sustained 
weak subsidence with high static stability, but a confluent stream 
of milder Gulf-modified air will hold just west of southwest Lower 
Michigan. Forecast soundings highlight a dry column, with PWATs 
dropping to around 0.25 inches. Insufficient boundary-layer 
saturation for a diurnal cumulus response, but given the upstream 
wave, high cirrus should spill in aloft with varying density. 
Thermodynamically, 850 mb temperatures appear relatively steady 
today, if not marginally warmer than Tuesday. Daytime highs should 
reach the mid-upper 50s. Upper level clouds thicken tonight while 
lower tropospheric theta-e advection works in late tonight from the 
west.

The speed max is expected to sharpen as it cross The UP and into 
Ontario Thursday, featuring a vertically stacked area of low 
pressure through 300 mb. Southeast Michigan becomes positioned 
between the surface low over central Ontario and high pressure over 
the Mid-Atlantic. This leads to a tightening pressure gradient 
resulting in an uptick in prevailing winds. Tenuous stability should 
limit the window of opportunity for lower column winds to 
effectively mix down and produce higher magnitude gusts. However, 
during the diurnal peak, should mixing depths tap into the 3-5 kft 
AGL layer, some 30-40 knots of flow would be available for gusts in 
excess of 30 mph. The low's extended cold front washes out over 
central Lower, which prevents a material wind shift toward the west 
and maintains a dry forecast. The next ridge axis works in Thursday 
night into Friday offering a more zonal orientation aloft. The jet 
resides to the north into the weekend as the next Pacific trough 
works through the Four Corners. The next chance for rain comes 
Sunday as the embedded Pacific wave ejects across the Plains. Lots 
of moving parts to contend with given the subtropical storm along 
the southern Atlantic coast and a meandering low moving south across 
the Canadian Prairies that interferes with the jet pattern. Highs 
rise into the 60s during the weekend. Colder weather returns early 
next week.

&&

.MARINE...

As low pressure exits the northern Plains late Wednesday, an 
increase in the pressure gradient over Lake Huron looks to lead to a 
modest increase in southwest winds, despite the mild air mass (850 
mb temps of 5 to 7 C) working through. Thus, another round of Small 
Craft Advisories appears likely for tonight into Thursday. There 
still does not appear to be enough of an increase in low level 
moisture to support any rain activity through the workweek. A ridge 
axis tracking through on Friday will lead to light winds. Another 
strong low is expected to track just northwest of Lake Superior 
Friday night, allowing at least moderate south-southwest winds to 
develop by Saturday. Forecast uncertainty ramps up to finish the 
weekend into Monday, as ensemble members and operational medium 
range models differ on whether a secondary low will develop over the 
Midwest and track through northern Michigan. A handful of solutions 
suggest marginal northwest gales could come into play Sunday night 
in the wake of the low.
